# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Itohara_2019_tacrolimus_pbpk"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Itohara_2019_tacrolimus_pbpk"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12420> (open access; the
  Supplementary Information holds Table S2, the Simcyp equations and the final
  NONMEM control stream)

Itohara et al. built a minimal PBPK model of tacrolimus in Simcyp v17 and
re-encoded it in NONMEM so that a time-varying graft-liver size could be added.
The structure is a one-compartment model with first-order oral absorption; the
physiology lives in how clearance and bioavailability are *computed*:

* **Clearance** is a well-stirred hepatic extraction (SI Eq. 4 and 7) of an
  intrinsic clearance built from recombinant-CYP kinetics for two CYP3A4 and two
  CYP3A5 pathways (13-O-desmethylation and 12-hydroxylation), scaled by hepatic
  enzyme abundance, microsomal protein and liver weight (SI Eq. 1).
* **Liver regeneration** (main-text Eq. 1, the selected model): the graft is 60%
  of the recipient's standard liver size at surgery and recovers hyperbolically
  with a half-recovery time of one postoperative day,
  `LW = (GR + (1 - GR) / (1 + 1/POD)) * LWstd`.
* **Bioavailability** is `F = Fa x Fg x Fh`, with `Fa` designated 0.6 and a
  Qgut gut-wall model (SI Eq. 5) whose CYP3A Michaelis-Menten extraction
  saturates on the portal-vein concentration.
* **Genotype**: hepatic CYP3A5 follows the *donor* (graft) genotype and
  intestinal CYP3A5 the *recipient* genotype. The paper's four groups are
  L\*1/I\*1, L\*1/I\*3, L\*3/I\*1 and L\*3/I\*3 (L = graft liver, I = recipient
  intestine, \*1 = CYP3A5\*1 carrier, \*3 = CYP3A5\*3/\*3), i.e.
  `CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR` and `CYP3A5_EXPR` in this model.

# Population

Model building used 26 adult LDLT recipients at Kyoto University Hospital
(December 2013 - January 2016; mean age 53.5 years, mean weight 66.6 kg, mean
hematocrit 25.5%) with routine TDM concentrations during the initial
intravenous infusion and oral troughs. Verification used 272 adult LDLT
recipients (July 2004 - June 2011; mean age 52.2 years, mean weight 60.1 kg)
with trough concentrations over the first 28 postoperative days. Donor
CYP3A5 \*3/\*3 / \*1/\*3 / \*1/\*1 counts were 14 / 11 / 1 (building) and
166 / 92 / 14 (verification); recipient counts were 15 / 9 / 2 and 171 / 88 / 13
(Table S1). All simulations in the paper used 100 Simcyp Japanese virtual adults
per genotype combination on the 2013 Kyoto protocol: intravenous tacrolimus
1.25 ug/h/kg for 12 h, then 0.83 ug/h/kg, switched on POD 3 to oral
0.04 mg/kg/day.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Itohara_2019_tacrolimus_pbpk")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source; the
table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Liver regeneration `f_regen = gr + (1 - gr) POD/(POD + 1)` | n/a | Main-text Eq. 1 (selected; lowest SQE, P < 0.001 vs Eq. 2-4); control stream `LV` |
| `gr` | 0.6 | Methods 'GR was assumed to be 60%'; control stream `LVD=LVR*0.6` |
| Hepatic CLint (SI Eq. 1) | n/a | SI Eq. 1; control stream `CLIL` (constant 1080 = liver density g/L, 0.00006 = 1e-6 x 60) |
| Well-stirred CL and Fh | n/a | SI Eq. 4, 7; control stream `TVCL`, `FH` |
| Gut CLint and Fg (SI Eq. 2, 5) with two-step saturable refinement | n/a | SI Eq. 2, 5; control stream `CLIG`, `INI`, `CLIGI`, `CPV`, `CLIGM`, `FGA` |
| `F = Fa x Fg x Fh` | n/a | SI 'Bioavailability F is the product of Fa, Fh and Fg'; control stream `F1` |
| `Vd = vc x WT` | n/a | SI Eq. 6 |
| `lka` | log(4.48) | **Not in the paper**; Ji 2018 Table 2 (see Assumptions) |
| `fa` | 0.6 | Results 'PBPK modeling' (smallest RMSE) and 'Simulation' |
| `lvc` | log(1.29) L/kg | Table S2 'Vb'; Methods |
| `fu`, `bpr`, `fu_gut` | 0.013, 35, 1 | Table S2 |
| `isef` | 0.24 | Table S2 (all pathways) |
| `vmax_*`, `km_*` (8 values) | 8, 0.21; 0.6, 0.29; 17, 0.21; 1.4, 0.35 | Table S2 (Dai 2006); control stream `CLIL` |
| `abund_cyp3a4_liver`, `abund_cyp3a5_liver` | 93, 17 pmol/mg | Table S2; Methods 'PBPK model development' |
| `mppgl_vliver` | 56.04 | **Back-solved** (see below) |
| `qco` | 251 L/h | **Back-solved** (see below) |
| `fq_liver_*`, `fq_pv_*` | 0.255 / 0.280, 0.19 / 0.215 | Control stream `B`, `C` |
| `qgut` | 11.4 L/h | Table S2 'Qgut' |
| `abund_cyp3a4_gut`, `abund_cyp3a5_gut` | 76585, 20283 pmol | **Back-solved** (see below) |
| `expSd` | 0.3162 | Control stream `$SIGMA 0.1`, `Y=F*EXP(EPS(1))` |
| No IIV | n/a | Control stream `$OMEGA 0 FIXED 0 FIXED` |

# Typical-value simulation

All validation below uses a typical 60 kg male recipient (the verification
cohort's mean weight; the cardiac output was back-solved for the male
hepatic-flow fraction) on the paper's standard protocol, one subject per
genotype combination. The model has no random effects, so these are exact
typical-value predictions.

```{r events}
mod <- readModelDb("Itohara_2019_tacrolimus_pbpk")

genotypes <- tibble::tibble(
  geno = c("L*1/I*1", "L*1/I*3", "L*3/I*1", "L*3/I*3"),
  CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR = c(1, 1, 0, 0),
  CYP3A5_EXPR = c(1, 0, 1, 0)
)

# Kyoto 2013 protocol: IV 1.25 ug/h/kg for 12 h, 0.83 ug/h/kg until POD 3,
# then oral 0.04 mg/kg/day as 0.02 mg/kg every 12 h. Doses in mg, time in h.
protocol_events <- function(id, wt, sexf, ld, ir, obs_times) {
  iv <- data.frame(
    time = c(0, 12),
    amt = c(1.25e-3 * wt * 12, 0.83e-3 * wt * 60),
    rate = c(1.25e-3 * wt, 0.83e-3 * wt),
    evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
  )
  po <- data.frame(
    time = seq(72, 28 * 24 - 12, by = 12),
    amt = 0.02 * wt, rate = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(iv, po, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      id = id, WT = wt, SEXF = sexf, POD = time / 24,
      CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR = ld, CYP3A5_EXPR = ir
    )
}

obs_grid <- seq(0, 28 * 24, by = 1)
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(genotypes)), function(i) {
  protocol_events(i, 60, 0, genotypes$CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR[i], genotypes$CYP3A5_EXPR[i], obs_grid) |>
    dplyr::mutate(geno = genotypes$geno[i])
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_typ[ev_typ$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))

# The model has no random effects, so rxode2's "multi-subject simulation
# without 'omega'" note below is expected: the subjects differ only in
# covariates.
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_typ, keep = "geno", returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(all(is.finite(sim_typ$Cc)))
```

## Back-solved inputs reproduce the paper's hepatic and gut outputs

Four `$INPUT` items of the control stream are Simcyp virtual-population outputs
whose values the paper does not print (see Assumptions). They were back-solved
from the paper's own reported outputs, so the comparison below is a
**self-consistency check of the back-solve, not an independent validation**:
two hepatic values (`mppgl_vliver`, `qco`) against six printed hepatic outputs,
and two gut abundances against the two printed `Fg` values.

```{r calibration}
at_time <- function(t) {
  sim_typ |>
    dplyr::filter(abs(time - t) < 1e-9) |>
    dplyr::distinct(geno, .keep_all = TRUE)
}
cl_pod <- function(pod) {
  # CL for a given POD from the model's own equations (deterministic).
  ev <- protocol_events(1, 60, 0, 1, 0, pod * 24)
  ev <- ev[ev$evid == 0, ]
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(ev, dplyr::mutate(ev, id = 2, CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR = 0))
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  stats::setNames(s$cl, c("L*1", "L*3"))
}
cl0 <- cl_pod(0)
cl30 <- cl_pod(30)
end <- at_time(660) # last oral dose (POD 27.5): F evaluated with its dose and trough

hep <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~published, ~model,
  "CL, L*1, POD 0 (L/h)", 0.975, cl0[["L*1"]],
  "CL, L*3, POD 0 (L/h)", 0.729, cl0[["L*3"]],
  "CL, L*1, POD 30 (L/h)", 1.59, cl30[["L*1"]],
  "CL, L*3, POD 30 (L/h)", 1.19, cl30[["L*3"]],
  "Fh, L*1", 0.979, end$fh[end$geno == "L*1/I*1"],
  "Fh, L*3", 0.985, end$fh[end$geno == "L*3/I*3"],
  "Fg, I*1 (mean over L)", 0.153, mean(end$fg[end$geno %in% c("L*1/I*1", "L*3/I*1")]),
  "Fg, I*3 (mean over L)", 0.227, mean(end$fg[end$geno %in% c("L*1/I*3", "L*3/I*3")])
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model / published - 1))

hep |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = signif(model, 4), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Quantity" = quantity, "Published" = published,
    "Model" = model, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Back-solve self-consistency (Results 'Simulation'; Discussion).")

# Deterministic: the back-solve reproduces every target to within 1.6%
# (measured maximum |difference| 1.6%).
stopifnot(nrow(hep) == 8L, all(abs(hep$pct_diff) < 2.5))
```

## Figure 6: CL, F and CL/F over the first postoperative month

```{r figure-6, fig.height = 7}
# F depends on the dose amount and the blood level at the dose, so it is read
# at the oral dose times (every 12 h from POD 3), where f(depot) applies.
fig6 <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 72, time < 28 * 24, abs(time %% 12) < 1e-9) |>
  dplyr::mutate(POD = time / 24, `CL/F (L/h)` = cl / f_oral) |>
  dplyr::select(geno, POD, `CL (L/h)` = cl, `F` = f_oral, `CL/F (L/h)`) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(geno, POD), names_to = "quantity")

ggplot(fig6, aes(POD, value, colour = geno, linetype = geno)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~quantity, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Postoperative day", y = NULL, colour = "Genotype", linetype = "Genotype",
    title = "Typical CL, F and CL/F after LDLT",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Itohara 2019 (typical 60 kg male, oral doses from POD 3)."
  )
```

CL depends only on the graft genotype and F almost only on the recipient
genotype, so pairs of lines overlap in those panels. Before the first oral dose
the model has no dose amount for the saturable gut term, so `F` is shown from
POD 3.

```{r figure-6-check}
f_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~geno, ~F_pub, ~CLF_pub,
  "L*1/I*1", 0.090, 17.0,
  "L*1/I*3", 0.131, 11.3,
  "L*3/I*1", 0.090, 11.8,
  "L*3/I*3", 0.131, 7.9
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    end |> dplyr::transmute(geno, F_model = f_oral, CLF_model = cl / f_oral),
    by = "geno"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    F_pct = 100 * (F_model / F_pub - 1),
    CLF_pct = 100 * (CLF_model / CLF_pub - 1)
  )

f_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(F_model, CLF_model), \(x) signif(x, 3)),
                dplyr::across(c(F_pct, CLF_pct), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Genotype" = geno, "F, published" = F_pub, "F, model" = F_model,
    "F diff (%)" = F_pct, "CL/F published (L/h)" = CLF_pub,
    "CL/F model (L/h)" = CLF_model, "CL/F diff (%)" = CLF_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "End-of-month F and CL/F (Results 'Simulation'; the paper prints one F per intestinal genotype).")

# F is Fa x Fg x Fh, all three pinned above: measured |diff| <= 2.8%.
# CL/F runs 6-10% high in every group: the paper reports the MEDIAN of the
# per-subject CL/F of 100 virtual subjects with log-normal CYP abundances,
# while CL and F were matched to its MEAN CL and median F; the gate allows 15%.
stopifnot(
  nrow(f_tab) == 4L, all(is.finite(f_tab$F_model)),
  all(abs(f_tab$F_pct) < 5),
  all(abs(f_tab$CLF_pct) < 15)
)
```

sim_typ |>

## Figure 5: trough concentration/dose ratios

The paper verified the model against observed trough C/D ratios
((ng/mL)/(mg/kg/day)) in three weekly windows and printed the predicted medians
for POD 22-28: 102, 155, 167 and 244 for L\*1/I\*1, L\*1/I\*3, L\*3/I\*1 and
L\*3/I\*3. The model's only between-subject inputs are weight and sex, so the
virtual cohort below (100 per genotype, the paper's number) varies those
alone; weight is drawn from the verification cohort's mean (SD) of 60.1 (12.3)
kg and half the subjects are female (sex was not reported).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190828)
n_per <- 100L
cohort <- tidyr::expand_grid(genotypes, k = seq_len(n_per)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = seq_len(dplyr::n()),
    WT = pmin(pmax(stats::rnorm(dplyr::n(), 60.1, 12.3), 35), 100),
    SEXF = stats::rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 0.5)
  )
trough_times <- seq(72 + 11.99, 28 * 24, by = 12)
ev_coh <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
  protocol_events(
    cohort$id[i], cohort$WT[i], cohort$SEXF[i],
    cohort$CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR[i], cohort$CYP3A5_EXPR[i], trough_times
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(geno = cohort$geno[i])
}))
sim_coh <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_coh, keep = c("geno", "WT"), returnType = "data.frame")

cd <- sim_coh |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    POD = time / 24,
    window = cut(POD, c(8, 15, 22, 29), right = FALSE, labels = c("POD 8-14", "POD 15-21", "POD 22-28")),
    cd = Cc / 0.04
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(window))

ggplot(cd, aes(geno, cd)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~window) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Trough C/D ((ng/mL)/(mg/kg/day))",
    title = "Trough C/D ratio by genotype and week",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates the predicted boxes of Figure 5 of Itohara 2019",
      "(spread from weight and sex only)."
    )
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

```{r figure-5-check}
cd_tab <- cd |>
  dplyr::filter(window == "POD 22-28") |>
  dplyr::group_by(geno) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cd_model = stats::median(cd), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tibble(geno = genotypes$geno, cd_pub = c(102, 155, 167, 244)),
    by = "geno"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (cd_model / cd_pub - 1))

cd_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(cd_model = round(cd_model), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Genotype" = geno, "Median C/D, model" = cd_model,
    "Median C/D, published" = cd_pub, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Predicted median trough C/D, POD 22-28 (Results 'Model verification').")

# Centre-of-distribution gate: the ordering
# L*1/I*1 < L*1/I*3 ~ L*3/I*1 < L*3/I*3 is structural and the medians must lie
# within 25% of the paper's (measured +6% to +17%; the L*1 groups run highest,
# see Assumptions). Weight and sex barely move the median, so the bound has
# headroom on any cohort draw.
stopifnot(
  nrow(cd_tab) == 4L,
  all(abs(cd_tab$pct_diff) < 25),
  cd_tab$cd_model[cd_tab$geno == "L*1/I*1"] < cd_tab$cd_model[cd_tab$geno == "L*3/I*3"]
)
```

## Table 1: genotype-guided starting doses

The paper derived three doses from the final model: an intravenous loading
rate that brings the concentration to 15 ng/mL at 12 h, a maintenance rate that
holds 15 ng/mL from POD 0.5, and an oral daily dose that holds a 10 ng/mL
trough at POD 3. They are recomputed below for the typical 60 kg male. The
oral dose is found by root-finding because the saturable gut makes `F`
depend on the dose; it is the steady-state trough with POD held at 3.

```{r table-1}
one_subject <- function(ld, ir, ev) {
  ev |> dplyr::mutate(id = 1, WT = 60, SEXF = 0, CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR = ld, CYP3A5_EXPR = ir)
}
# Loading: concentration at 12 h per 1 ug/h/kg is linear in the rate.
load_rate <- function(ld, ir) {
  ev <- data.frame(
    time = c(0, 12), amt = c(1e-3 * 60 * 12, 0), rate = c(1e-3 * 60, 0),
    evid = c(1L, 0L), cmt = "central"
  ) |>
    one_subject(ld = ld, ir = ir) |>
    dplyr::mutate(POD = time / 24)
  c12 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame")$Cc
  15 / c12
}
# Maintenance: CL at POD 0.5 x 15 ng/mL, per kg.
maint_rate <- function(ld, ir) {
  ev <- data.frame(time = 12, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central") |>
    one_subject(ld = ld, ir = ir) |>
    dplyr::mutate(POD = 0.5)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame")$cl * 15 / 60
}
# Oral: steady-state trough at POD 3 (30 days of q12h dosing, POD frozen).
trough_pod3 <- function(dose_mgkgday, ld, ir) {
  dose_t <- seq(0, 30 * 24 - 12, by = 12)
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = dose_t, amt = dose_mgkgday / 2 * 60, rate = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(time = 30 * 24, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    one_subject(ld = ld, ir = ir) |>
    dplyr::mutate(POD = 3)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  s$Cc[nrow(s)]
}
oral_dose <- function(ld, ir) {
  stats::uniroot(function(d) trough_pod3(d, ld, ir) - 10, c(0.005, 0.3), tol = 1e-6)$root
}

tab1 <- genotypes |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    load = load_rate(CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR, CYP3A5_EXPR),
    maint = maint_rate(CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR, CYP3A5_EXPR),
    oral = oral_dose(CYP3A5_EXPR_DONOR, CYP3A5_EXPR)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = oral / (maint * 24 / 1000)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      geno = genotypes$geno,
      load_pub = c(1.41, 1.41, 1.31, 1.31),
      maint_pub = c(0.309, 0.309, 0.230, 0.230),
      oral_pub = c(0.0662, 0.0446, 0.0468, 0.0306)
    ),
    by = "geno"
  )

tab1 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    geno,
    load = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", load, load_pub),
    maint = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", maint, maint_pub),
    oral = sprintf("%.4f (%.4f)", oral, oral_pub),
    ratio = sprintf("%.2f", ratio)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Genotype" = geno,
    "Loading, ug/h/kg: model (paper)" = load,
    "Maintenance at POD 0.5, ug/h/kg: model (paper)" = maint,
    "Oral at POD 3, mg/kg/day: model (paper)" = oral,
    "Oral / IV maintenance" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Recomputed Table 1 of Itohara 2019 (typical 60 kg male).")

tab1_pct <- with(tab1, 100 * c(maint / maint_pub - 1, oral / oral_pub - 1))
# Deterministic. Maintenance -2 to -5% and oral +5 to +14% measured. The
# loading rate is a known deviation (see below) and is not gated.
stopifnot(length(tab1_pct) == 8L, all(is.finite(tab1_pct)), all(abs(tab1_pct) < 20))
```

The maintenance and oral doses agree with Table 1 to within 14%. The loading
rate does not: the model needs about 1.70-1.74 ug/h/kg against the paper's
1.31-1.41. With `Vd = 1.29 L/kg` (Table S2, SI Eq. 6), raising the blood
concentration to 15 ng/mL within 12 h takes at least
`15 x 1.29 / 12 = 1.61 ug/h/kg` even with no elimination, so the printed
loading rates are not reachable with the paper's own volume; the paper's
L\*1 / L\*3 ratio (1.08) is also larger than its clearances can produce over
12 h. The difference is recorded here rather than resolved.

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. PKNCA is used here to confirm, from the simulated
profiles alone, that the apparent oral clearance over the last dosing interval
(POD 27-27.5, effectively steady state) matches the model's `CL/F` and the
paper's end-of-month `CL/F`.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= 648, time <= 660) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, geno)

# Dose in ug so that Dose / AUC (ug / (h x ng/mL)) comes out in L/h.
dose_df <- ev_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 648) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = amt * 1000) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, geno)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | geno + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | geno + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 648, end = 660,
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cl.last = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tibble(geno = f_tab$geno, cl.last = f_tab$CLF_pub)
# ncaParamLabel() has no friendly label for 'cl.last' and warns; the code is
# relabelled below, so only that warning is muffled.
cmp <- withCallingHandlers(
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = nca_res,
    reference = published,
    by = "geno",
    units = c(cl.last = "L/h"),
    tolerance_pct = 20
  ),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("unknown PKNCA code", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
cmp$`NCA parameter`[cmp$`NCA parameter` == "cl.last (L/h)"] <- "CL/F = Dose/AUCtau (L/h)"
stopifnot(nrow(cmp) == 4L)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "PKNCA over the last dosing interval vs published end-of-month CL/F. * differs from reference by >20%.")

as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "tmax", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::select(geno, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-geno, \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Genotype" = geno, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUCtau (h*ng/mL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated steady-state exposure on 0.02 mg/kg q12h, POD 27-27.5 (not reported by the paper).")

# Dose/AUCtau must equal the model's own CL/F at steady state (same solve,
# numerical error only; measured < 1%).
cl_last <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cl.last") |>
  dplyr::left_join(f_tab |> dplyr::select(geno, CLF_model), by = "geno")
stopifnot(nrow(cl_last) == 4L, all(abs(cl_last$PPORRES / cl_last$CLF_model - 1) < 0.03))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Absorption rate constant.** Itohara 2019 does not report `ka` (the `SKA`
  data item is a Simcyp output), and it cannot be recovered from SI Eq. 3:
  with the designated `Fa = 0.6`, `Fa = 1 - (1 + ka Tsi / 7)^-7` fixes only the
  product `ka x Tsi = 0.979`. The maintainers ratified using
  `ka = 4.48 1/h` from the adult LDLT tacrolimus model of Ji 2018
  (`Ji_2018_tacrolimus`, itself fixed from the literature). The paper's
  verification data are troughs, so `ka` shapes only the absorption phase and
  the absorbed-flux part of the saturable gut term; with `ka = 4.48 1/h` that
  term is roughly half of the portal-vein concentration at the dose, so a
  different `ka` would shift `Fg` by several percent.
- **`Fa` is a designated constant.** The control stream computes `FA` from
  `SKA` and `TSI` by SI Eq. 3, but the paper fixed `Fa` at 0.6 for the final
  model; it is encoded directly and `Tsi` is not needed.
- **Back-solved Simcyp inputs.** Cardiac output, microsomal protein per gram of
  liver, standard liver volume and the whole-gut CYP3A4 / CYP3A5 abundances
  are per-subject Simcyp outputs that the paper does not print. The
  maintainers back-solved typical values from the paper's own outputs (never
  from Simcyp defaults):
  - `qco = 251 L/h` and `mppgl_vliver = 56.04` by least squares on the six
    printed hepatic outputs (CL at POD 0 and 30 and Fh, for L\*1 and L\*3);
    only the product of microsomal protein and liver volume is identifiable.
    `qco` corresponds to a hepatic blood flow of 64.0 L/h with the male
    fraction 0.255; it is applied to both sexes because the sex-specific
    Simcyp cardiac outputs are not reported, so the female hepatic flow here
    is 10% higher than the male one (effect on CL < 0.5%).
  - The gut abundances (`abund_cyp3a4_gut = 76585 pmol`,
    `abund_cyp3a5_gut = 20283 pmol` for a CYP3A5\*1 recipient) so that the
    model's saturable `Fg` at the last oral dose of the standard regimen
    (POD 27.5, 60 kg male, averaged over graft genotypes) equals the printed
    0.227 (I\*3) and 0.153 (I\*1). The control stream tabulates the saturable
    `FGA`, not the linear `FG`; matching the linear form instead gives 67121
    and 19856 pmol and a saturable `Fg` about 13% above the paper's.
  - The printed hepatic CYP3A5 abundance (17 pmol/mg) is the expresser value;
    non-expresser grafts carry 0. This is what reproduces both the L\*1 and
    L\*3 clearances with one `mppgl_vliver`.
- **Km units.** Table S2 renders the Km unit as 'mM'. The control stream's
  unit factor `0.00006 = 1e-6 x 60` only works for Km in umol/L, so umol/L
  is used.
- **No between-subject variability.** The control stream fixes both etas to
  zero; the paper's between-subject spread came from Simcyp virtual-population
  draws (only the hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP3A5 abundance CVs, 81% and 185%, are
  reported). The model is a typical-value predictor; the Figure 5 cohort
  varies weight and sex only and is much narrower than the paper's boxes.
- **Weight and liver size.** Clearance does not scale with body weight here,
  because liver volume and microsomal protein enter only as their back-solved
  typical product; in Simcyp the standard liver volume scales with body
  size.
- **Systemic concentration in the gut term.** The control stream adds the
  previous record's simulated observation `Y` (which includes the residual
  error under `$SIM`) to the portal-vein concentration; the model uses the
  noise-free blood concentration at the dose time. The `exp(-KA*TAD)` factor
  is 1 at the dose record, where bioavailability is evaluated.
- **Sex mix and typical weight.** Table S1 does not report sex. The typical
  subject is a 60 kg male; the Figure 5 cohort is half female.
- **Remaining differences.** CL/F runs 6-10% above the paper's medians and the
  L\*1 C/D medians differ most, because the paper summarises 100 Simcyp
  subjects with log-normal enzyme abundances (medians of ratios) whereas this
  model was matched to the paper's mean CL. The paper itself is not fully
  consistent here: the Discussion quotes Fh of 0.967 / 0.976, the Results
  0.979 / 0.985; the Results values are used. The Table 1 intravenous loading
  rates are not reproduced (model about 25% higher; see the Table 1 section).
- **Errata.** EuropePMC lists no correction notice for this article
  (PMID 31087501) as of 2026-10-16.
